content:
We got a list of templates. Need to find which one, when applied to the target molecule, reproduces the reaction (i.e., gives precursors). The template IDs are not given directly; we have reaction_id fields. The required output: mapped_rxn string and template_id (the one used to search the database not the hash). Likely template_id corresponds to reaction_id? In earlier tasks, template_id is integer. So we can pick one of these that matches Friedel-Crafts acylation. Look at each template's retro_smarts: they involve breaking halide (Cl) attached to aromatic carbon and forming amide carbonyl attached to aromatic nitrogen? Actually the target molecule has an amide linking aromatic ring to heterocycle: "NC(=O)c2nnn(... )c2Cl". The acyl group is attached to aromatic ring via amide nitrogen? Wait structure: COc1cccc(NC(=O)c2nnn(Cc3ccc(CN4CC(F)C4)cc3)c2Cl)c1. So we have an anilide: aromatic ring with -NH-CO- attached to a heterocycle (c2nnn...). The heterocycle has a Cl substituent. The Friedel-Crafts acylation would be attaching an acyl group onto aromatic ring, but here the acyl group is attached to nitrogen (amide). Hmm maybe the transformation is from an acyl chloride (R-CO-Cl) reacting with an aniline to give amide (acylation of amine). That's not Friedel-Crafts but acylation of amine. However description says electrophilic aromatic substitution, halide removed. Could be that the aromatic ring originally had a Cl substituent that is replaced by acyl group (acylation). In product we have a carbonyl attached to aromatic via nitrogen? Actually the carbonyl is attached to aromatic nitrogen (anilide). The aromatic ring is methoxy-substituted and has -NH-CO- attached. The carbonyl carbon is attached to heterocycle (c2nnn...). So the acyl group is attached to nitrogen, not directly to aromatic carbon. So maybe the reaction is not Friedel-Crafts but amide formation from acyl chloride and amine (acylation). The halide is from acyl chloride. So template should break halide (Cl) attached to carbonyl carbon and form amide bond (C=O attached to N). That matches templates where retro_smarts: [#7:2]-[C;H0;D3;+0:3](=[O;H0;D1;+0:1])-[c:4]...>>Cl-C... etc. The first template (reaction_id 153550) seems to have retro_smarts: '[#7:2]-[C;H0;D3;+0:3](=[O;H0;D1;+0:1])-[c:4]:[c:5]:[#7;a:6]>>Cl-C1=C(-Cl)-C(=[O;H0;D1;+0:1])-C(-C#N)=C(-C#N)-C-1=O.[#7:2]-[CH2;D2;+0:3]-[c:4]:[c:5]:[#7;a:6]'. This seems to involve a heteroaryl with Cl and nitrile groups, not our case.

Second template (761427) seems complex with many substituents.

Third (609618) retro_smarts: '[#7:5]-[C;H0;D3;+0:6](=[O;D1;H0:7])-[c;H0;D3;+0:1](:[#7;a:2]):[c:3]:[#7;a:4]>>Br-[c;H0;D3;+0:1](:[#7;a:2]):[c:3]:[#7;a:4].[#7:5]-[CH;D2;+0:6]=[O;D1;H0:7]'. This is bromide leaving, forming amide. That seems plausible: break C-Br, form amide. Our target has a Cl on heterocycle, not on carbonyl carbon. But the template expects halide attached to aromatic carbon (aryl halide). In our molecule, the heterocycle has a Cl attached to aromatic carbon of heterocycle (c2Cl). So that matches: aryl halide (aryl chloride) being replaced by amide carbonyl attached to nitrogen. So template 609618 could be appropriate.

Similarly template 1111246 is same but with Cl instead of Br.

Thus template_id likely 1111246 (reaction_id). The mapped_rxn is provided in entry: 'mapped_rxn': '...'.

We need to return mapped_rxn and template_id (integer). So choose template_id 1111246 and mapped_rxn from that entry.

Let's extract mapped_rxn string for 1111246. In the result, for 1111246 entry, mapped_rxn is:

'[CH3:1][CH:2]([CH3:3])[CH:4]1[CH2:5][N:6]([C:7]2=[N:8][C:9]([C:10](=[O:11])[N:12]([CH3:13])[CH3:14])=[CH:15][N:16]=[CH:17]2)[CH2:18][CH2:19][NH:20]1.Cl.CNC.CCN(CC)CC.C=O.[CH3:13][N:12]([CH3:14])[CH:10]=[O:11]>>[CH3:1][CH:2]([CH3:3])[CH:4]1[CH2:5][N:6]([c:7]2[n:8][c:9]([C:10](=[O:11])[N:12]([CH3:13])[CH3:14])[cH:15][n:16][cH:17]2)[CH2:18][CH2:19][NH:20]1'

But need to verify. The entry shows product and reactant sides. The mapped_rxn appears to have product on left? Usually mapped_rxn format is reactants>>products. In entry, seems left side includes many fragments including Cl etc, then >> product. That's fine.

Thus final answer: {'mapped_rxn': '[CH3:1][CH:2]([CH3:3])[CH:4]1[CH2:5][N:6]([C:7]2=[N:8][C:9]([C:10](=[O:11])[N:12]([CH3:13])[CH3:14])=[CH:15][N:16]=[CH:17]2)[CH2:18][CH2:19][NH:20]1.Cl.CNC.CCN(CC)CC.C=O.[CH3:13][N:12]([CH3:14])[CH:10]=[O:11]>>[CH3:1][CH:2]([CH3:3])[CH:4]1[CH2:5][N:6]([c:7]2[n:8][c:9]([C:10](=[O:11])[N:12]([CH3:13])[CH3:14])[cH:15][n:16][cH:17]2)[CH2:18][CH2:19][NH:20]1', 'template_id': 1111246}

Check if template_id is integer. Yes.

Return final answer.
